key_insight: Combining LLM-powered information extraction with an agent-based, multi-level reconstruction pipeline enables automated recovery of hierarchical structural architectures from distributed ROS 2 artifacts that previously only exposed node-level wiring implicitly.
problem_solved: Recovering hierarchical, component- and subsystem-level architecture from scattered ROS 2 sources (code, launch/config, manifests) is hard because composition and integration semantics are implicit and existing tools focus only on node-level communication.
method: Agent-based pipeline where specialized agents (parsers, LLM extractors, fusers) process ROS 2 artifacts to identify entities, interfaces, and composition relations.
Multi-level reconstruction: fuse cross-artifact signals to build layered representations (nodes → components → subsystems) and resolve ambiguous links via LLM reasoning and structural heuristics.
Iterative validation and human-in-the-loop corrections to refine the hierarchical model and produce standard architecture views usable for analysis and evolution.
impact: Enables practitioners to automatically obtain meaningful architecture models for robotic ML systems, improving program comprehension, automated testing, simulation setup, and evolution planning—reducing manual effort and error when working with complex ROS 2 deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: artifacts (source, launch, configs) → specialized agents → fusion → multi-level architecture output
Before/after comparison: flat node-level wiring vs reconstructed hierarchical components/subsystems
Example reconstructed hierarchy: tree or UML-like view showing nodes grouped into components and subsystems with interfaces
Icon set: ROS 2 node, launch file, LLM/agent, and validation/checkmark to convey inputs and capabilities
paper_title: Towards LLM-Assisted Architecture Recovery for Real-World ROS~2 Systems: An Agent-Based Multi-Level Approach to Hierarchical Structural Architecture Reconstruction
paper_authors: Dominique Briechle, Raj Chanchad, Tobias Geger, Ruidi He, Dhruv Jajadiya
